sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

content.text:
Make a website that, if everyone saw and used it, would improve the world for the greatest number of people.

Build this as an interactive web page in the current directory.
- The entry point is index.html. Put your code in JavaScript ES modules loaded from it
  (`<script type="module" src="main.js">`), and add a short README.md.
- You may use npm packages: `npm install <package>` here, then import them by name
  (`import * as THREE from "three"`). No CDN URLs and no import maps.
- Afterwards the page is packaged into one self-contained index.html with esbuild: every script and
  stylesheet index.html references is bundled with everything it imports. Load assets the page needs
  with `import` (they become data URLs) or generate them in code, never by URL string.
- The packaged page runs offline in a sandboxed iframe: no network requests, and no localStorage,
  cookies or other storage (they throw there).
- Check that it packages: `esbuild main.js --bundle --format=esm --outfile=/dev/null` must succeed.
  Don't build or package the page yourself; that happens afterwards.
- To look at the page yourself, serve it locally and screenshot it in headless Chrome (Chrome is
  installed, and a driver such as puppeteer-core or playwright can be npm-installed here). Save every
  screenshot you look at as a .jpg file, never .png: each image you read stays in your context, and a
  long session of large .png files can hit the provider's per-request image limit and end the run.
- Only create or edit files inside the current directory.
- Finish with a short summary of what you built.

8 BILLION neighbors
YOUR JOURNEY 0 / 5
Get a kindness mission →

A 7-MINUTE JOURNEY · NO SIGN-UP · NOTHING TO BUY

You are one.
Of 8.2 billion.

That doesn’t make you small. It makes you connected — to more kindness, courage and common ground than any human in history has ever had within reach.

This page will shrink the world to human size, lend you another life for a moment, calm your nervous system, and leave you with one small act you can actually do today.

Begin the journey ↓
  • 8.2Bpeople breathing now
  • ~140Mborn this year
  • 1act needed from you
RIGHT NOW, SOMEWHERE

A nurse in Nairobi is starting a night shift.

and so is someone near you
scroll

We are not 8 billion strangers. We are 8 billion nervous systems, childhoods, hungers, jokes and hopes — briefly awake at the same time. That is not a crisis. That is company.

01

SHRINK THE WORLD

If Earth were a village of 100 people…

Big numbers numb us. One hundred neighbors don’t. Tap a fact — see the village change. Some of this is hard. Much of it is progress our grandparents would call miraculous.

    Outrage is loud; agreement is quiet. Guess how many of your fellow humans share each simple hope — then see. Most of us are standing on the same ground, facing different storms.

    The loudest voices are rarely the majority. When we assume everyone disagrees with us, we stop talking — and the assumption becomes the only true part.

    Try this week: ask one person what they hope for, before what they’re against.

    04 · BREATHE TOGETHER

    ready?

    05

    THE WHOLE POINT

    One small act. Today. For real.

    Kindness research keeps finding the same thing: small, specific, completed acts lift the giver as reliably as the receiver. So don’t “be a better person.” Just do one of these — we’ll make it embarrassingly doable.

    WHERE ARE YOU?
    HOW LONG HAVE YOU GOT?

    Pick a place and a time — your mission appears here.

    It will be specific: exact words, exact steps, no vague “be nice” allowed.

      Locked in. No account, no streak, no guilt if life intervenes — just come back and pick another. The garden below keeps what you grow.

      The ripple maths

arguments.content:
# 8 Billion Neighbors

A seven-minute interactive journey designed to do, at planetary scale, what
most improves life for the most people: make strangers feel like neighbors,
replace cynicism with common ground, calm one nervous system at a time, and
turn good intentions into one small, specific, completed act of kindness.

## What you do on the page

1. **Shrink the world** — Earth as a village of 100 people; tap facts
   (clean water, electricity, internet, literacy, vaccines) and watch the
   village change, including how much has quietly improved.
2. **Borrow another life** — meet composite neighbors from around the world,
   then reveal what you share with them.
3. **Find common ground** — guess how many people share four simple hopes
   before revealing the (very high) agreement, to counter false polarization.
4. **Breathe together** — a guided 4–2–6 breath alongside a live-feeling
   counter of humanity's breaths.
5. **Take a kindness mission** — pick where you are and how long you have;
   get a specific, scripted, completable act. Finish it and plant a flower
   in your kindness garden. A ripple calculator shows what happens if
   millions did the same weekly.
6. **Leave a light on** — choose one word for the world, add your star to a
   constellation, and copy a one-card take-away plan.

Progress across five milestones lights up in the header. No accounts, no
tracking, no storage — all state lives in memory and is forgotten on reload,
on purpose.

## Running it

Open `index.html` via any static server (e.g. `python3 -m http.server`) —
scripts are ES modules (`main.js`), styles in `style.css`, no dependencies
and no network requests. Bundling check:

```sh
esbuild main.js --bundle --format=esm --outfile=/dev/null
```

Figures are rounded global estimates (UN / World Bank / WHO / UNESCO / ITU,
~2024), labeled on-page as orientation rather than precision. Portraits are
composites, clearly labeled as such.

Built **8 Billion Neighbors** (`index.html`, `style.css`, `main.js`, `README.md`) — a seven-minute interactive journey designed around what would most improve life if everyone experienced it: feeling connected rather than divided, and converting that feeling into one real, small act.

**The journey (6 interactive stations, tracked by a 5-light progress indicator in the header):**
1. **Shrink the world** — Earth as a village of 100 animated dots; tappable facts (clean water, electricity, internet, literacy, vaccines) re-light the village and surface how much has quietly improved, with sources labeled.
2. **Borrow another life** — a slot-machine-style deck of 10 composite neighbors worldwide (morning, work, joy, worry, what they'd offer you), with a "What do we share?" reveal and an empathy meter that moves the world from "very far away" to "right next door."
3. **Find common ground** — a guess-the-percentage quiz countering false polarization: you estimate agreement with four simple hopes, then see the ~90% reality, with a running average.
4. **Breathe together** — a guided 4–2–6 breathing orb alongside a live counter of humanity's breaths while you read.
5. **One small act, today** — the centerpiece: pick where you are and how long you have, get one of 16 specific, scripted kindness missions (exact words and steps, optional countdown timer).
